correctness.rationale: Takloo-Bighash's explicit normalized coefficient bound is uniform enough once r log(2r)=o(sqrt(ell)): the largest test prime satisfies P=O_D(r log r), hence P^2=o(ell), and Stirling makes the Fourier errors negligible even after determinant perturbation. Exact Vandermonde cancellation bounds every competing auxiliary determinant by P^(2r) times the main one, while the adjacent-prime exponential is suppressed by exp(-ell/P). All parity, nonvanishing-normalizer, and weight-range hypotheses persist for the growing block.

originality.rationale: The motivating preprint proves only fixed-r independence and explicitly does not optimize dependence on r. Kayath--Lane--Neifeld--Ni--Xue conjecture a much larger linear-size independent family but provide only finite computational checks, while Ni--Xue's related period theorem also fixes the number of periods. Searches did not identify a prior theorem allowing r to grow under r log r=o(sqrt(ell)) or an equivalent near-square-root initial block. The source is extremely recent, so unindexed contemporaneous work remains the main residual risk.

value.rationale: The result upgrades a qualitative fixed-block theorem to an explicit growing family of size almost sqrt(ell)/log(ell), giving structural progress toward the conjectural linear-size Rankin-Cohen basis. The proof identifies a reusable quantitative mechanism: exact Vandermonde ratio control plus uniform Fourier-error decay. The novelty is not presented as a best possible L-value counting bound, especially in the untwisted D=1 case where stronger counting results are known.
